title: Problem 5.1 (cover-free families)
context_text: A family of sets $\mathcal{F}$ is $(w,r)$-cover-free if for all $A_1,\dots,A_w\in\mathcal{F}$ and all $B_1,\dots,B_r\in\mathcal{F}\setminus\{A_1,\dots,A_w\}$ one has $\bigcap_{i=1}^w A_i\not\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^r B_i$; in particular $(1,r)$-cover-free means that no set of the family is covered by the union of $r$ other sets. $\mathcal{P}(t)$ denotes the power set of a $t$-element ground set, and $t(n,w,r)$ is the minimum $t$ such that some $(w,r)$-cover-free family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(t)$ has $n$ sets. Known bounds give $\Omega(r^{w+1}\log n/\log r)\le t(n,w,r)\le\mathcal{O}(r^{w+1}\log n)$ for fixed $w$ and $r$ not too large ($r=\mathcal{O}(n^{w/(w+1)})$); for $w=1$ the lower bound $t(n,1,r)=\Omega(\min\{n, r^2\log n/\log r\})$ is due to D'yachkov–Rykov and Füredi, and the authors extend it to $t(n,w,r)=\Omega(\min\{n^w,r^{w+1}\log n/\log r\})$ for fixed $w$. The question asks whether the lower bound is tight for $w=1$, closing the longstanding $\log r$ gap. The motivation in the paper is graph reconstruction with maximal independent set queries (each query is a vertex set $Q$ and the answer is a maximal independent set of $G[Q]$): the minimum number of queries of a deterministic non-adaptive algorithm reconstructing every $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ lies between $t(n,2,2\Delta-2)$ and $t(n,2,2\Delta)$, which yields the bounds $\Omega(\Delta^3\log n/\log\Delta)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^3\log n)$, with the same gap.
notes: Parser assigned the label 'Problem 5.0' to all three problems in Section 5; this is likely Problem 5.1 or the first of several unnumbered problems.
paper_title: Lower bounds for graph reconstruction with maximal independent set queries

title: Problem 5.2 (randomised non-adaptive optimality)
statement_text: Is there a randomised non-adaptive algorithm which uses $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^{2}\log(n/\Delta))$ maximal independent set queries to reconstruct any graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ with high probability?
context_text: In graph reconstruction with maximal independent set (MIS) queries, an algorithm must determine all edges of a hidden graph $G$ on a known vertex set $V$ of size $n$, where each query is a set $Q\subseteq V$ and the answer is some maximal independent set of the induced subgraph $G[Q]$ (chosen by an adversary). An algorithm is non-adaptive if its queries are fixed in advance, adaptive if each query may depend on previous answers; a randomised algorithm need only succeed with high probability (lower bounds are for success probability at least $1/2$). Konrad, O'Sullivan and Traistaru showed that $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^2\log n)$ random non-adaptive queries reconstruct graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ with high probability, and that $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^3\log n)$ deterministic non-adaptive queries suffice. The authors prove that every randomised non-adaptive algorithm needs $\Omega(\Delta^2\log(n/\Delta))$ queries (and every randomised adaptive one $\Omega(\Delta^2\log(n/\Delta)/\log\Delta)$, answering a question of Konrad, O'Sullivan and Traistaru who had shown $\Omega(\Delta^2+\log n)$). The question asks whether the non-adaptive lower bound is tight, i.e. whether the gap between $\log n$ and $\log(n/\Delta)$ can be closed.
notes: Parser assigned the label 'Problem 5.0' to all three problems in Section 5; this is likely Problem 5.2 or the second of several unnumbered problems.

title: Problem 5.3 (adaptive vs non-adaptive gap)
statement_text: Is there a deterministic adaptive algorithm that uses $o(\Delta^{3}\log(n/\Delta))$ maximal independent set queries to reconstruct any graph of maximum degree $\Delta$?
context_text: In graph reconstruction with maximal independent set (MIS) queries, an algorithm must determine all edges of a hidden graph $G$ on a known vertex set $V$ of size $n$, where each query is a set $Q\subseteq V$ and the answer is some maximal independent set of the induced subgraph $G[Q]$ (chosen by an adversary). An algorithm is non-adaptive if its queries are fixed in advance, adaptive if each query may depend on previous answers; a randomised algorithm need only succeed with high probability (lower bounds are for success probability at least $1/2$). Konrad, O'Sullivan and Traistaru showed that $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^2\log n)$ random non-adaptive queries reconstruct graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ with high probability, and that $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^3\log n)$ deterministic non-adaptive queries suffice. In fact their argument gives $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^3\log(n/\Delta))$ deterministic non-adaptive queries, and the authors prove that deterministic non-adaptive algorithms need $\Omega(\Delta^3\log n/\log\Delta)$ queries (via cover-free families). For adaptive algorithms the known upper bounds are the same as in the non-adaptive case, while the best lower bound drops to $\Omega(\Delta^2\log(n/\Delta)/\log\Delta)$ in both the deterministic and randomised settings. This gap suggests that adaptive algorithms might perform better than non-adaptive ones, which the question asks to confirm in the deterministic case.
